_: The model files the installed app fetches on its first start. NOTICE says
which they are and under what terms.
`urls` is tried in order. `url` (and `inside`) is the PUBLISHER's address,
kept for launchers from before 1.0.3, which read only that and behave as
they always did. In `urls` the first is the project's own mirror - a
`models` release on the project's repository, uploaded once by hand - and
the publisher's address follows where there is one. The mirror came first
the day an installed copy could reach GitHub but not Hugging Face, and the
AnimeText and Manga109 routes stayed gray with no way to fix it short of
copying files by hand. lee: *"fix it in the download file, i dont want to
have the user run these"*. The COO sound-effect weights have no fetchable
publisher address at all (a shared drive), so the mirror is their only
line, and `url` names it too. The two webtoon models are NOT mirrored:
their publisher never wrote a licence down (NOTICE), and their GitHub
address answers everywhere the mirror would.
`tier` decides what happens when one cannot be had. `required` stops the
start with a message and stops a release; `recommended` is logged, the
route that wanted it stays gray in the editor until it can be had, and a
release goes out anyway.
`sha256` is the file every measurement in this project was made on, taken
from lee's own copies; a file that arrives different is refused, on the
way in and at release time. `tools/release.py models` fetches every one
of these from the first address that answers and says which, if any, no
longer matches.
